subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: telling a trusted adult right away [Action]
passage:
Monday night. Ganga sat on her bed with the phone face down. It buzzed again and again. She felt ashamed and alone, and every time she thought of telling somebody, her throat closed. She didn't sleep.
Tuesday morning. At breakfast she said, “Mummy, something happened,” and the words came out in pieces. Mummy put her spoon down, held her, and said, “Thank you for telling me. This is not your fault.” They rang the school before eight.
Thursday. Sarita ma'am, the class teacher, met them with the safety lead. Together they wrote a plan: who would be told, what would be saved, and who would check on Ganga each day. Ganga's shoulders came down from around her ears for the first time in days.

qa.q: How did Ganga feel on Monday night?
qa.a: Ashamed and alone: her throat closed each time she thought of telling somebody.

qa.q: What was the turning point, and why did it help?
qa.a: Telling Mummy at breakfast, because it turned a secret carried alone into a plan shared with adults.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Sarita ma'am?
qa.a: Sarita ma'am meets a frightened student and her mother after a call, and wants to protect Ganga and follow the school's process without blaming her.

grounding: A teen tells her mother and class teacher what happened, despite shame, and they plan next steps together.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: telling a trusted adult right away [Action]
passage:
Lokesh, sit. You asked why I pushed you to tell me about those messages. Let me tell you why.
When I was fifteen, a boy in my class took a photo of me on the school trip, changing my shoes behind the bus, and passed it round on phones with an ugly caption. I found out on a Tuesday. I felt so ashamed I wanted the ground to swallow me. I thought, if I tell Amma, she'll look at me differently.
But that night I told her anyway, crying into her sari. She didn't ask why I was behind the bus. She said, “This is not your shame, Sudha.” Next morning she took me to Mrs Iyer, my class teacher. The three of us sat together and made a list: who had the photo, who to speak to, what the principal must do.
It wasn't easy. But I wasn't carrying it alone any more. So now, show me those messages.

qa.q: What did Amma say when Sudha told her?
qa.a: This is not your shame, Sudha.

qa.q: What was young Sudha afraid of before telling Amma?
qa.a: Sudha felt deeply ashamed and was afraid Amma would look at her differently.

qa.q: What choice in the story changed things for Sudha?
qa.a: Telling Amma that night despite the shame, which led to Mrs Iyer and a shared plan instead of carrying it alone.

qa.q: How might Amma have felt hearing Sudha's story that night?
qa.a: Amma was likely hurt and angry on Sudha's behalf, but steady, making sure Sudha knew the shame was not hers.

grounding: An elder recalls telling her mother and class teacher about a humiliating shared photo despite shame, and planning the next steps together.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: telling a trusted adult right away [Action]
passage:
Amma was in Chennai for a work training, and the rain was so heavy that the video call kept freezing. Urmila had rehearsed it three times in the bathroom. Someone had posted a screenshot of her private chat with a friend, the one about her crush, in the class group, with laughing comments under it.
“Amma, something happened. I feel stupid telling you.”
The picture froze on Amma's face, then came back. “Tell me slowly.”
Urmila did, eyes on the floor. Amma listened to the end. “You're not stupid. Forward me the screenshots now. Tomorrow, first period, you go to Reena Ma'am. I'll call her tonight so she knows before you walk in.”
At nine, Reena Ma'am phoned. “Your mother told me. Come to the staffroom before assembly. We'll decide the next steps together, the three of us.”
Urmila slept better than she had expected.

qa.q: Where was Amma when Urmila told her?
qa.a: In Chennai, for a work training.

qa.q: How was Urmila feeling before telling Amma?
qa.a: Urmila felt ashamed and stupid, rehearsing three times in the bathroom and keeping eyes on the floor.

qa.q: Why was telling Amma, despite the distance, a good step?
qa.a: Amma could act that same night by calling Reena Ma'am, so Urmila didn't face school alone the next morning.

qa.q: How might Reena Ma'am see the evening call?
qa.a: Reena Ma'am gets warning before school and can plan with Urmila and Amma, instead of hearing about it after more harm.

grounding: Shows a teen telling her mother and class teacher about a leaked private chat despite feeling ashamed, and the three of them planning next steps together.
